Name: Welcome-to-the-AI-Hub
Title: Welcome to the Cassin AI Hub
Description: One place for prompts, Friday tips, videos and agents.
Html:
The AI Hub is the firm's home for getting more out of Microsoft 365 Copilot. You'll find:

  • Prompt Library: prompts written for our deals and documents, from term sheet comparisons to closing checklists. Add your own.
  • Friday Tips: every weekly tip, with the steps, the prompt and a video.
  • Demo Videos: short walkthroughs for Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams and Copilot Chat.
  • Agents & Tools: Daily Digest, the Email Filing Assistant and what's coming next.

The site is run by the AI Working Group with Fortify Cyber. If something's missing, use Feedback and tell us.

Name: Meet-Daily-Digest
Title: Meet Daily Digest: your inbox, sorted before you start
Description: A morning summary of what needs you, from your own mailbox.
Html:
Daily Digest is a Copilot agent that reads your inbox and gives you a short morning briefing: 🔴 high priority, 📨 waiting on your reply, 👥 team items you're copied on, and 📰 updates, with marketing and cold outreach filtered out.

To try it: open Daily Digest in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams or Outlook and say "Run my daily digest". To get it every weekday, schedule that prompt once. It takes about five minutes.

It only reads your own mailbox, with your own sign-in, and the only email it can send is your digest, to you.

Name: Email-Filing-Assistant-Pilot
Title: Email Filing Assistant: suggest, never auto-move
Description: What the pilot is testing and how it was designed with the team.
Html:
After the AI Working Group's feedback, the Email Filing Assistant follows a few firm rules:

  • It only suggests a folder for emails you've already dealt with.
  • You confirm every filing. Nothing moves on its own.
  • It never touches flags or categories.
  • It's optional. If you don't use folders, you don't have to use it.

A small pilot group is testing it now. If you'd like to join, or have thoughts on how filing should work, let us know.
_comment: Pilot news belongs to the AI Working Group, not the firm-wide hub. Remove: true deletes the post (to the site recycle bin) on the next run.

Name: Copilot-for-Legal
Title: New from Microsoft: legal skills in Copilot for Word
Description: Contract review, redlining, defined terms and more, built into Word for Copilot users.
Html:
Microsoft has released Copilot for Legal: more than 20 legal skills built into Copilot, for summarizing, drafting, reviewing and redlining legal documents. It's included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot license everyone at Cassin already has.

What it can do

  • Review and redline an agreement against a playbook or precedent, with suggested edits applied as normal Word tracked changes.
  • Check the drafting: defined terms, cross-references and key terms across agreements.
  • Summarize a redline or compare terms between documents.
  • Track obligations: pull out commitments, deadlines and triggers.

Make sure it's on (30 seconds)

  1. Open Word on your computer (the desktop app) and select Copilot.
  2. In the Copilot pane, select the three dots in the top-right corner, then Manage plugins & skills.
  3. Confirm Legal is turned on.

There's also a legal version for Cowork, Microsoft's workspace for longer, multi-step tasks. It's a separate plugin, and the AI Working Group will let you know when it's set up at Cassin.

Before you rely on it

Review every suggested edit yourself, as you would a junior's markup, and follow the firm's AI Acceptable Use Policy and the client AI opt-out list.

Source: Microsoft's announcement (October 15, 2026).
